text:
Can you write the pitch for our crowdfunding campaign? I chair the volunteer group trying to reopen the one-screen cinema in our town of 6,500. It closed in 2022.

Facts:
- We need $85,000 to replace the projector and sound system and fix the roof. The building's owner has agreed to rent it to us for $1 a year for 10 years if we raise it.
- We ran a campaign 3 years ago for $120,000. It reached $47,000 and we refunded everyone.
- This time a local bank has pledged $25,000 if we raise the rest by June 30.
- 46 volunteers have signed up to run the box office and the snack bar.
- When it closed, the cinema was selling about 180 tickets a week.
- The nearest other cinema is 38 miles away.

Keep it under 350 words.

Before I draft this, a few questions. Each answer changes what the pitch says:

1. **What's the crowdfunding target, and what happens if you miss it?** I'm reading the bank's $25,000 as part of the $85,000, which would leave $60,000 to raise from the public. Is that right? Is the deadline June 30, 2027? If you fall short, do backers get refunded like last time?

2. **What are the cinema and the town called, and is there one detail locals will remember?** For example, the year it opened, a well-known feature, or a memory people mention.

3. **Why did the last campaign fall short, and can we say so openly?** Many of your likely backers gave last time and got refunded, so they'll be wondering about it. Naming it head-on (smaller target, bank match, $1 lease, 46 volunteers) is probably your strongest move, but only if you're comfortable with that.

4. **How will the cinema pay its way once it's open?** Donors will ask whether it'll close again. A rough sense of yearly running costs compared with what about 180 tickets a week brings in would help, even if it's only a ballpark.

5. **Are there reward tiers or concrete things a donation buys?** For example, "$100 names a seat" or "$500 covers a month of roof repairs." If you haven't set any yet, I'll leave them out.

If you don't know some of these, just say so. I'll write around the gaps rather than guess.

1. Yes, $60,000 from the public, with the bank's $25,000 counting toward the $85,000. The deadline is June 30, and the campaign opens May 1. It's all-or-nothing: if we don't reach $85,000 by June 30, every pledge is returned in full.

2. It's the Majestic on Main Street. I don't have a specific detail like the year it opened.

3. I don't know exactly why it fell short. Yes, say it openly. This goal is $35,000 lower than last time.

4. I don't know the running costs.

5. No reward tiers yet, so leave them out.

Ruth Albers

I'm holding to all-or-nothing in the draft, and I didn't invent any running costs or other details you didn't give me. It's about 290 words.

<final_document>
**Bring the Majestic Back**

The Majestic on Main Street has been dark since 2022. The nearest cinema is now 38 miles away, so a night at the movies means a 76-mile round trip.

We're the volunteers working to reopen it. We need to raise $60,000 by June 30.

**What your pledge pays for**

Reopening will cost $85,000. That buys a new projector and a new sound system and fixes the roof. A local bank has pledged $25,000 if we raise the other $60,000 by June 30. If we do, the building's owner will rent us the Majestic for $1 a year for ten years.

**We've tried before**

Three years ago we asked for $120,000. We raised $47,000, fell short and refunded every dollar. Many of you gave then, and we haven't forgotten that.

This time is different:

- **The goal is $35,000 lower.**
- **The bank's pledge covers nearly a third of the cost.**
- **Rent is $1 a year for ten years.**
- **46 volunteers have already signed up** to run the box office and the snack bar.

**The town still wants its cinema**

When the Majestic closed, it was still selling about 180 tickets a week. People here didn't stop going to the movies. The town lost its cinema.

**All or nothing**

The campaign runs from May 1 to June 30. If pledges and the bank's $25,000 don't reach the full $85,000, every pledge is returned in full. Your money only goes into the project if we can finish it.

Pledge what you can, then tell a neighbor. We need $60,000, and we hope to see you in the seats.

Ruth Albers
Chair, on behalf of the Majestic volunteers
</final_document>

- **Running costs:** Backers will ask whether the cinema can stay open this time. Once you have even a rough yearly running cost, one line comparing it with ticket income from about 180 tickets a week would answer that.
- **Sign-off:** I didn't know your group's formal name, so I wrote "the Majestic volunteers." Swap in the real name if there is one.
- **Opening date:** The pitch doesn't say when the Majestic would reopen. If you have a target date, adding it would make the ask more concrete.
